lessons.title: Terminal Commands & Navigation
lessons.theory: Bash shell cho Linux/macOS. Terminal commands quản lý files, processes, networking. Cần thiết cho mọi developer. WSL cho Windows.
lessons.code:
# Navigation
pwd                          # print working directory
ls -la                       # list all files (detailed)
cd ~/projects                # change directory
mkdir -p src/components      # create nested dirs

# File operations
touch index.js               # create file
cp file.txt backup.txt       # copy
mv old.js new.js             # rename/move
rm -rf node_modules          # remove recursively

# File content
cat README.md                # print file
head -20 log.txt             # first 20 lines
tail -f server.log           # follow live log
less large-file.txt          # paginated viewer

# Search
grep -rn "TODO" src/         # search text in files
find . -name "*.js" -type f  # find files by name
which node                   # find command location

# Pipes & Redirect
ls -la | grep ".js"          # pipe output
echo "hello" > file.txt      # write (overwrite)
echo "world" >> file.txt     # append
cat file.txt | wc -l         # count lines

# Process
ps aux | grep node           # find processes
kill -9 <PID>                # force kill
top                          # system monitor
df -h                        # disk usage
free -h                      # memory usage
keyPoints: | pipe: output cmd1 → input cmd2
> overwrite, >> append, 2> stderr redirect
grep -rn: recursive search with line numbers
lessons.exercise: Navigate filesystem: create project structure, find/search files.

lessons.title: Cơ bản về lập trình kịch bản Bash Shell
lessons.theory: Bash scripts automate tasks. Variables, conditionals, loops, functions. Exit codes. Command substitution $(cmd). String operations.
lessons.code:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail  # strict mode: exit on error

# Variables
NAME="DevMaster"
COUNT=$(ls -1 | wc -l)
DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
echo "Hello $NAME, $COUNT files today ($DATE)"

# Conditionals
if [ -f "package.json" ]; then
    echo "Node.js project detected"
    npm install
elif [ -f "requirements.txt" ]; then
    echo "Python project"
    pip install -r requirements.txt
else
    echo "Unknown project type"
fi

# String comparison
ENV="${1:-development}"  # default value
if [[ "$ENV" == "production" ]]; then
    echo "⚠️  Production deployment!"
fi

# Loops
for file in *.js; do
    echo "Processing: $file"
    # do something with $file
done

for i in {1..5}; do
    echo "Iteration $i"
done

# Functions
log() {
    local level="${1:-INFO}"
    local msg="$2"
    echo "[$(date +%H:%M:%S)] [$level] $msg"
}

log "INFO" "Script started"
log "WARN" "Check your config"

# Exit codes
if command -v docker &>/dev/null; then
    log "INFO" "Docker available"
else
    log "ERROR" "Docker not found"
    exit 1
fi
keyPoints: set -euo pipefail: strict mode, fail on any error
${1:-default}: parameter with default value
$(): command substitution, capture output
lessons.exercise: Viết script setup project: detect type, install deps, configure.

lessons.title: Text Processing: awk, sed, xargs
lessons.theory: Unix text processing power: awk (column extraction), sed (stream editor), xargs (build commands from input). Combine cho powerful data pipelines.
lessons.code:
#!/bin/bash

# awk - column extraction & processing
ps aux | awk '{print $1, $11}'        # user + command
df -h | awk 'NR>1 {print $5, $6}'     # usage + mount
cat data.csv | awk -F"," '{sum+=$3} END {print "Total:", sum}'

# sed - stream editor (find/replace)
sed -i 's/http:/https:/g' urls.txt           # replace in file
sed -n '10,20p' log.txt                      # print lines 10-20
cat config.yml | sed 's/debug: true/debug: false/'

# xargs - pass input as arguments
find . -name "*.tmp" | xargs rm               # delete all .tmp
cat urls.txt | xargs -P 4 -I {} curl -s {}    # parallel curl
git diff --name-only | xargs wc -l            # line count changed files

# Combined pipeline
# Find top 10 largest files
find . -type f -exec du -h {} + | sort -rh | head -10

# Count TODO/FIXME per file
grep -rn "TODO\|FIXME" src/ | \
  awk -F: '{print $1}' | \
  sort | uniq -c | sort -rn

# Log analysis: top IPs
cat access.log | \
  awk '{print $1}' | \
  sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20

# JSON processing with jq
curl -s https://api.github.com/users/octocat | \
  jq '{name: .name, repos: .public_repos, followers: .followers}'
keyPoints: awk: column extraction -F"," cho CSV, {print $1}
sed: s/old/new/g replace, -i cho in-place edit
xargs -P N: parallel execution, powerful with find/grep
lessons.exercise: Analyze log file: top errors, traffic by hour, slow requests.

lessons.title: Viết kịch bản tự động hóa & Lập lịch với Cron Job
lessons.theory: Automate deployments, backups, monitoring. Cron jobs schedule. SSH remote commands. Environment management.
lessons.code:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Deploy script
deploy() {
    local ENV="${1:-staging}"
    local BRANCH="${2:-main}"
    local TIMESTAMP=$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)
    local DEPLOY_DIR="/var/www/app"
    local BACKUP_DIR="/var/backups/app"

    echo "🚀 Deploying $BRANCH to $ENV..."

    # Backup current
    if [ -d "$DEPLOY_DIR" ]; then
        tar -czf "$BACKUP_DIR/backup_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz" "$DEPLOY_DIR"
        echo "✅ Backup created"
    fi

    # Pull & build
    cd "$DEPLOY_DIR"
    git fetch origin
    git checkout "$BRANCH"
    git pull origin "$BRANCH"

    # Install & build
    npm ci --production
    npm run build

    # Restart
    pm2 restart app --update-env
    echo "✅ Deployed $BRANCH to $ENV"

    # Health check
    sleep 5
    if curl -sf http://localhost:3000/health > /dev/null; then
        echo "✅ Health check passed"
    else
        echo "❌ Health check failed! Rolling back..."
        rollback "$TIMESTAMP"
        exit 1
    fi
}

rollback() {
    local TIMESTAMP="$1"
    tar -xzf "/var/backups/app/backup_$TIMESTAMP.tar.gz" -C /
    pm2 restart app
    echo "🔄 Rolled back to $TIMESTAMP"
}

# Cron examples (crontab -e)
# 0 2 * * * /scripts/backup.sh        # daily 2 AM
# */5 * * * * /scripts/health-check.sh # every 5 min
# 0 0 * * 0 /scripts/cleanup.sh        # weekly Sunday

deploy "$@"
keyPoints: Deploy scripts: pull → build → restart → health check → rollback
Cron: minute hour day month weekday command
trap cho cleanup: trap "rm -f $TMPFILE" EXIT
lessons.exercise: Viết deploy script với rollback, health check, notifications.

lessons.title: Giám sát hệ thống Linux & Khắc phục sự cố
lessons.theory: Server monitoring: CPU, memory, disk, network. Log analysis. Performance troubleshooting. Health check scripts.
lessons.code:
#!/bin/bash

# System status dashboard
status() {
    echo "=== System Status ===$(date) ==="
    echo ""
    echo "📊 CPU: $(top -bn1 | grep "Cpu(s)" | awk '{print $2}'% used)"
    echo "💾 Memory: $(free -h | awk '/Mem:/ {print $3 "/" $2}')" 
    echo "💿 Disk: $(df -h / | awk 'NR==2 {print $3 "/" $2 " (" $5 " used)"}')" 
    echo "🌐 Network: $(ss -tuln | grep -c LISTEN) listening ports"
    echo "📦 Containers: $(docker ps -q 2>/dev/null | wc -l) running"
    echo ""

    # Process check
    for service in nginx node postgres redis; do
        if pgrep -x "$service" > /dev/null; then
            echo "✅ $service running"
        else
            echo "❌ $service NOT running"
        fi
    done
}

# Alert if thresholds exceeded
check_alerts() {
    local CPU=$(top -bn1 | grep "Cpu(s)" | awk '{print int($2)}')
    local MEM=$(free | awk '/Mem:/ {print int($3/$2 * 100)}')
    local DISK=$(df / | awk 'NR==2 {print int($5)}')

    [ "$CPU" -gt 90 ] && alert "CPU usage: ${CPU}%"
    [ "$MEM" -gt 85 ] && alert "Memory usage: ${MEM}%"
    [ "$DISK" -gt 90 ] && alert "Disk usage: ${DISK}%"
}

alert() {
    local MSG="$1"
    echo "⚠️  ALERT: $MSG"
    # curl -X POST "$SLACK_WEBHOOK" -d "{\"text\": \"$MSG\"}"
}

# Log analysis
analyze_logs() {
    local LOG="${1:-/var/log/app/access.log}"
    echo "=== Log Analysis ==="
    echo "Total requests: $(wc -l < "$LOG")"
    echo "Errors (5xx): $(grep -c ' 5[0-9][0-9] ' "$LOG")"
    echo "Top endpoints:"
    awk '{print $7}' "$LOG" | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -5
}

status
keyPoints: pgrep: check if process running by name
free -h / df -h: human-readable memory/disk info
Combined awk + sort + uniq -c: frequency analysis
lessons.exercise: Xây monitoring dashboard: status checks, alerts, log analysis.

lessons.title: Bash nâng cao: Mảng, Bắt tín hiệu Traps & Mạng
lessons.theory: Bash arrays, associative arrays. Signal traps cho cleanup. SSH automation. Here documents. Process substitution.
lessons.code:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Arrays
SERVERS=("web1" "web2" "web3" "db1")
for server in "${SERVERS[@]}"; do
    echo "Checking $server..."
    ssh "$server" "uptime" 2>/dev/null || echo "  ❌ $server unreachable"
done
echo "Total servers: ${#SERVERS[@]}"

# Associative array (map)
declare -A CONFIG
CONFIG[host]="localhost"
CONFIG[port]="5432"
CONFIG[db]="myapp"
for key in "${!CONFIG[@]}"; do
    echo "$key = ${CONFIG[$key]}"
done

# Trap (cleanup on exit)
TMPDIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $TMPDIR; echo Cleaned up" EXIT INT TERM

# Here document
cat > "$TMPDIR/config.yml" <<EOF
app:
  name: myapp
  port: 3000
  env: ${ENV:-development}
EOF

# Process substitution
diff <(ssh web1 "cat /etc/config") <(ssh web2 "cat /etc/config")

# Parallel execution
max_parallel=4
running=0
for server in "${SERVERS[@]}"; do
    deploy_to "$server" &
    ((running++))
    if [ "$running" -ge "$max_parallel" ]; then
        wait -n  # wait for any one to finish
        ((running--))
    fi
done
wait  # wait for remaining
keyPoints: ${ARRAY[@]}: all elements, ${#ARRAY[@]}: length
trap "cleanup" EXIT: guaranteed cleanup on exit
<<EOF heredoc: multi-line strings with variable substitution
lessons.exercise: Viết parallel deployment script cho multiple servers.

lessons.title: Bảo mật Shell Script & Tối ưu hiệu năng thực thi
lessons.theory: High-performance scripting, security best practices, portable scripts. Race condition handling, atomic operations, secure temp files.
lessons.code:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

# Security: never use eval with user input
# ❌ eval "$USER_INPUT"
# ✅ Use case/if for controlled execution

# Secure temp files
TMPFILE=$(mktemp /tmp/myapp.XXXXXX)
trap "shred -u $TMPFILE 2>/dev/null" EXIT

# Atomic file write (prevent partial writes)
atomic_write() {
    local target="$1"
    local tmpfile="${target}.tmp.$$"
    cat > "$tmpfile"
    mv -f "$tmpfile" "$target"  # atomic on same filesystem
}
echo "new config content" | atomic_write /etc/myapp/config

# Lock file (prevent concurrent execution)
LOCKFILE="/var/lock/myapp.lock"
exec 200>"$LOCKFILE"
if ! flock -n 200; then
    echo "Another instance running. Exiting."
    exit 1
fi

# Performance: avoid subshells
# ❌ Slow: VAR=$(echo "$string" | grep -c "pattern")
# ✅ Fast: [[ "$string" == *pattern* ]] && ((count++))

# ❌ Slow: for file in $(find . -name "*.js"); do
# ✅ Fast: find . -name "*.js" -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d "" file; do

find . -name "*.log" -print0 | while IFS= read -r -d "" file; do
    echo "Processing: $file"
done

# Portable: check OS
case "$(uname -s)" in
    Linux*)  OS="linux" ;;
    Darwin*) OS="macos" ;;
    MINGW*|MSYS*) OS="windows" ;;
    *) OS="unknown" ;;
esac
echo "Running on: $OS"
keyPoints: flock: prevent concurrent script execution
Atomic writes: write to tmp then mv (prevents corruption)
find -print0 + read -d "": handle filenames with spaces
lessons.exercise: Viết secure deployment script: lockfile, atomic ops, audit logging.
